$comment: The pre-alert board as a process owner would first draw it from the SOP,
before any AI review. Deliberately incomplete — the holes below are what
round 1 has to find, and they are the holes a careful reader of that SOP
would actually leave.
Three of these stop the board entering review, and they are all the drawing
not yet being a workable process: an outcome with no line out of it, and two
steps it stops at without ever saying so. A person fixes those on the canvas.
Everything else is a value only the process owner can supply, so it is the
reviewer's question rather than a refusal.
Left out on purpose:
· no recipients on the COA report     the SOP never says who receives it
· no system on the invoice report     the SOP says 'log an error', not where
· neither report marked as an ending  the SOP stops; nobody said the process does
· no idempotency_key on either        a resumed shipment would report twice
· no on_missing_input on either check nothing says what to do while waiting
· no deadline on the event            nothing bounds the wait
· mismatched_coa has no edge          the SOP names the outcome, not the path
· no sample_extracted yet             samples come from the fixture pull
· no output entity                    the SOP describes no result row at all
· nothing reads prealert_email.sender the report has to go somewhere, and
'whoever sent it' is a guess until asked
One problem is logged and the other emailed, because the SOP genuinely says
'log an error' for invoices and 'reported via email' for COAs. Whether that
asymmetry is real is a question for the process owner, not an assumption to
quietly resolve here.
Entities are primitives with primitive_type 'entity'. They carry no layout
entry, which is what makes them attachable rather than drawn.

config.name: Pre-alert email
config.identified_by: it arrives in the pre-alert group mailbox the bot has access to
config.instructions: The SOP says documentation must be reported by email but never says to whom. The sender is the obvious candidate and is deliberately not assumed here. One email carries a subject and a list of attachments, and the attachments are what there are several of; that a shipment gets several emails over days is a fact about the trigger rather than about what an email is.

config.name: Commercial Invoice
config.instructions: The invoice number is in the top-right corner.

config.name: Certificate of Analysis
config.identified_by: the page header reads "Certificate of Analysis"

config.name: Pre-alert documents received
config.match_condition: subject contains "Pre-Alert Documents" or "APL USA // PRE-ALERT DOCUMENTATION"
config.instructions: Sent by the exporter's clearing agent. Documents arrive in pieces — a shipment may get several emails, and corrected COAs come days later.

config.name: Does every line item include HTS, FDA product code, NDC and ANDA?
config.instructions: Review the "Description of Goods" section and make sure every line item carries all four identifiers.

config.name: Log the invoice error
config.instructions: Log an error naming the invoice number, the drug description and which information type is missing.

config.name: Does every batch on the invoice have a matching COA?

outcomes.name: missing_coa
outcomes.description: a batch on the invoice has no COA

outcomes.name: mismatched_coa
outcomes.description: a COA exists but its batch number disagrees

config.instructions: Each batch should have its own COA. Cross-check each batch listed on the invoice against a corresponding COA document.

config.name: Report the COA discrepancy
config.instructions: Report missing or mismatched COAs by email with the invoice number, the batch numbers and a description of the discrepancy.
